steps.say: The classic prostate operation shaves the adenoma away through a scope, and the original version runs on a fluid that conducts no electricity. Monopolar TURP washes the field with hypoosmolar fluid, either one point five percent glycine or sorbitol mannitol mixes, because plain salt water scatters the cutting current. That fluid choice is the root of the operation's famous complication, which the next step covers.
steps.tx: Perform **monopolar TURP** (classic single circuit prostate shaving) under non-conductive hypoosmolar irrigation with **1.5% glycine** (one point five percent glycine) or sorbitol and mannitol mixes, because saline would disperse the cutting current. The resectoscope loop shaves the obstructing adenoma lobes chip by chip while the fluid keeps vision clear. Every trainee links this fluid to **TUR syndrome** (dilutional collapse from absorbed wash), detailed next.

vis.alt: Diagram comparing normal prostate with BPH enlarged prostate lobes.
vis.caption: Normal vs BPH prostate: the obstructing adenoma lobes that TURP resects chip by chip. Credit: bank image.

steps.say: TUR syndrome is triggered when litres of glycine wash flood the bloodstream through open prostatic veins. The patient develops acute hypervolemic hyponatremia, meaning too much water with too little salt, plus confusion, visual blurring, and a slow pulse. Treatment is fluid restriction, diuretics, and slow correction with 3 percent hypertonic saline, never plain water, while watching the sodium climb safely.
steps.tx: Recognise **TUR syndrome** (wash absorption collapse) as acute **hypervolemic hyponatremia** (water overload with low sodium) with encephalopathy (confusion), visual disturbances, and bradycardia (slow pulse) during or after monopolar resection. Treat with fluid restriction, loop diuretics, and **3% hypertonic saline** (three percent strong salt water) for severe symptomatic lows. Prevention beats cure: limit resection time, keep the bag low, and switch negotiations to bipolar for big glands.

rows: Glycine wash absorbed via open veins
Short time, low bag, bipolar for big glands

steps.say: The bipolar upgrade keeps the same operation but changes the physics and the fluid. Bipolar TURP runs the current between two electrodes at the loop tip, creating a plasma corona that vaporises tissue in normal isotonic saline. Because the wash is ordinary 0.9 percent salt water, absorbed fluid cannot dilute the sodium, and the dreaded dilutional hyponatremia of TUR syndrome is completely eliminated.
steps.tx: Choose **bipolar TURP** (twin electrode prostate shaving) in **isotonic saline** (normal salt water, **0.9% NaCl**), where the loop tip **plasma corona** (glowing vapour layer) resects tissue while wash absorption stays harmless. Dilutional hyponatraemia cannot occur in salt water, so **TUR syndrome** (dilutional collapse) is completely eliminated. Bipolar is now the default for larger glands, longer resections, and patients with cardiac limits on fluid shifts.

steps.say: For huge glands the laser does not shave but peels. Holmium laser enucleation finds the plane between adenoma and surgical capsule and shells the whole obstructing lobes out intact, whatever the prostate size. The freed lobes are pushed into the bladder and chewed up by a morcellator, a spinning blade sucker, giving complete tissue for pathology with barely any bleeding.
steps.tx: Enucleate any size gland with **HoLEP** (holmium laser shelling, holmium laser enucleation of the prostate), dissecting the entire adenoma along the **surgical capsule** (gland outer rind) regardless of prostate size, then extracting chips by mechanical **tissue morcellation** (spinning blade mincing inside the bladder). Enucleation removes all obstructing tissue with minimal bleeding and full pathology, so size limits that bind TURP do not bind HoLEP.

vis.alt: Diagram of normal and BPH prostate showing zonal anatomy and adenoma position.
vis.caption: Prostate zonal anatomy: HoLEP shells the adenoma off the surgical capsule plane. Credit: bank image.

steps.say: The thulium laser is the precise younger sibling, cutting with a continuous wave instead of pulses. ThuLEP slices with exact control and seals as it goes, with a coagulation depth of only zero point one to zero point two millimetres, so surrounding tissue barely feels the heat. That shallow footprint makes it the safest enucleation for men who cannot stop their blood thinners.
steps.tx: Pick **ThuLEP** (thulium laser shelling, thulium laser enucleation) for precise continuous-wave cutting with superior coagulation at a **coagulation depth** (heat spread) of only **0.1 to 0.2 mm** (zero point one to zero point two millimetres). The shallow burn keeps bleeding trivial, so men on oral **anticoagulation** (blood thinners) undergo enucleation without stopping therapy. Outcomes match HoLEP with arguably smoother learning for laser beginners.

steps.say: Some men fear the operation's price on ejaculation more than the stream itself, and that fear is answered by the prostatic urethral lift. UroLift fires tiny suture implants through the lateral lobes that pin them back like curtain tiebacks, opening the channel with zero heat and zero cutting. Ejaculatory and erectile function are completely preserved, trading maximal flow gain for minimal harm.
steps.tx: Offer **prostatic urethral lift** (**UroLift**, suture pin prostate opening) to men prizing **ejaculatory preservation** (keeping normal ejaculation): transprostatic implants retract the lateral lobes without thermal injury, fully preserving ejaculatory and erectile function. Flow improves less than after resection, so select moderate obstruction with bothersome ejaculation concerns, and counsel that retreatments outnumber TURP failures.

steps.say: Steam treatment is delivered gently but it ablates tissue precisely. Water vapour thermal therapy, marketed as Rezum, needles radiofrequency generated steam at 103 degrees Celsius into the transition zone and the median lobe, where trapped heat kills cells that the body then resorbs over weeks. Done under local anaesthesia in minutes, it suits frail men wanting an office procedure with preserved sexual function.
steps.tx: Inject convective steam with **Rezum** (**water vapor therapy**, radiofrequency steam ablation) at **103 deg C** (one hundred three degrees) into transition zone tissue and the **median lobe** (middle obstructing hump), causing cellular necrosis with later resorption. The office procedure under local anaesthesia suits frail or anticoagulated men, preserves sexual function, and shrinks obstruction over weeks as dead tissue melts away.

rows: Water vapor therapy at 103 deg C

steps.say: When the adenoma has outgrown every scope, the open operation is still indicated. Simple prostatectomy, through Freyer transvesical or Millin retropubic routes, or their laparoscopic and robotic copies, shells giant benign adenomas above 80 to 100 cubic centimetres when no enucleation expert is available. It cures obstruction with the biggest recovery bill, so reserve it for glands lasers cannot reach in your hands.
steps.tx: Reserve **simple prostatectomy** (open adenoma shelling) via **Freyer transvesical** (through the bladder) or **Millin retropubic** (behind the pubis) routes, open, laparoscopic, or robotic, for massive adenomas exceeding **80 cc to 100 cc** (eighty to one hundred cubic centimetres) without enucleation expertise. The operation removes every obstructing gram at the cost of the longest recovery, so it stands last in the ladder after TURP, lasers, and office therapies.
